dmm-2013-tiebreaker-01.prompt: A light beam shines from the origin into the unit square at an angle of $\theta$ to one of the sides such that $\tan\theta=\frac{13}{17}$. The light beam is reflected by the sides of the square. How many times does the light beam hit a side of the square before hitting a vertex of the square? (The figure shows an example trajectory for $\tan\theta=\frac23$.)

dmm-2013-tiebreaker-02.prompt: Alex is given points $A_1,A_2,\dots,A_{150}$ in the plane such that no three are collinear and $A_1,A_2,\dots,A_{100}$ are the vertices of a convex polygon $P$ containing $A_{101},A_{102},\dots,A_{150}$ in its interior. He proceeds to draw edges $A_iA_j$ such that no two edges intersect (except possibly at their endpoints), eventually dividing $P$ into triangles. How many triangles are there?

dmm-2013-tiebreaker-03.prompt: The polynomial $P(x)$ has the property that $P(1),P(2),P(3),P(4)$, and $P(5)$ are equal to $1,2,3,4,5$ in some order. How many possibilities are there for the polynomial $P$, given that the degree of $P$ is strictly less than $4$?
